settings_dbsync.heading: Database Sync
settings_dbsync.intro: Save the current dev DB as a snapshot, and apply it to production on deploy.
settings_dbsync.import_confirm: This will TRUNCATE all data in the current database and replace it with the snapshot. This action cannot be undone. Continue?
settings_dbsync.import_success: Snapshot imported successfully ({{executed}} of {{total}} statements applied).
settings_dbsync.no_snapshot: No snapshot found yet. Run Step 1 below to generate one.
settings_dbsync.step1_desc_before: Exports the entire current database to
settings_dbsync.step1_desc_after: . This file is automatically applied to production on deploy.
settings_dbsync.step1_duration_note: Export dumps the entire current database. It can take 30 seconds to 2 minutes depending on database size.
settings_dbsync.export_disabled_prod: Export is disabled because the API is connected to a production database. Run Step 1 from the development environment only.
settings_dbsync.step2_title: Step 2 — Import snapshot into current DB
settings_dbsync.step2_desc: Applies the saved snapshot to the current database immediately. In a production environment, this writes to the production database.
settings_dbsync.step2_warning: all existing data will be deleted and replaced with the snapshot data. This action cannot be undone.
settings_dbsync.workflow_step1: In the development environment, run Step 1: Generate DB snapshot.
settings_dbsync.workflow_step2: Publish (deploy) → the production server automatically imports the snapshot on start-up if it has changed.
settings_dbsync.workflow_step3: Use Step 2 only if you need to re-apply the snapshot manually (for example, on a freshly-reset prod DB).
